content: The text provided is a detailed set of instructions for editing and updating references, URLs, and content in a document, specifically related to guidelines for drinking-water quality. 1. On page 419, under the Petroleum Products principal reference, update the citation from WHO (2005) to WHO (2008). 2. On page 419, under the Sulfate principal references, update the citation from WHO (2003) to WHO (2004). 3. On page 429, under the principal references, add the following reference below the IPCS (2004) reference: USNTP (1987). Toxicology and carcinogenesis studies of bromodichloromethane in F344/N rats and B6C3F1 mice (gavage studies). 4. On page 431, under the Uranium principal reference, update the citation from WHO (2011) to WHO (2012). 5. On page 432, under the Vinyl Chloride principal references, update the citation from WHO (2003) to WHO (2004). 6. Insert the following reference below Pathogenic mycobacteria in water: Pharmaceuticals in drinking-water. Published in 2012 by the World Health Organization. This document provides evidence-based, practical guidance and recommendations for managing pharmaceuticals in drinking-water. 7. On page 446, insert the following reference above Rapid assessment of drinking-water quality: Quantitative microbial risk assessment: application for water safety management. Published in 2016 by the World Health Organization. This document synthesizes current knowledge on quantitative microbial risk assessment (QMRA) to facilitate its application in water supply, water reuse, and water recreation, supporting the management of risks associated with fecal pathogens in water-related contexts. 8. Update the URL for Safe drinking-water from desalination to: http://www.int/water_sanitation_health/publications/toxicyanobact/en/ 9. Insert the following reference below Toxic cyanobacteria in water: Turbidity: information for regulators and operators of water supplies. Published in 2017 by the World Health Organization. This document provides information on the uses and significance of turbidity, intended for regulators and operators of drinking-water supplies. 10. Insert the following reference below Water safety in buildings: Water safety in distribution systems. Published in 2014 by the World Health Organization. This reference tool is designed to help water suppliers and regulators familiar with the water safety plan approach to enhance risk assessment, management, and investment planning for their water distribution systems. 11. Update the URL for Water treatment and pathogen control to: http://www.int/iris/handle/10665/63260 12. On page 457, update the citation from WHO (2003) to WHO (2004) for the references on Copper, DDT and its derivatives, Dialkyltins, Dimethoate, and Endosulfan. Move these references to page 460. 13. Delete the following reference: WHO (2003). Diquat in drinking-water. 14. On page 458, update the citation from WHO (2003) to WHO (2004) for the references on Endrin, Epichlorohydrin, Fenitrothion, Fluoride, Halogenated acetonitriles, Hexachlorobenzene, and Inorganic tin. Move these references to page 460. 15. Update the citation from WHO (2003) to WHO (2005) for the Glyphosate and AMPA reference. Move this reference to page 461, following the Formaldehyde reference. 16. Delete the following reference: WHO (2003). MCPA in drinking-water. 17. On page 460, update the citation from WHO (2003) to WHO (2004) for the references on Sulfate and Vinyl Chloride. Move these references as indicated. 18. Insert all WHO (2004) references below the WHO (2003) Zinc in drinking-water reference, in alphabetical order. 19. Insert the following reference below the WHO (2005) 1,4-Dioxane in drinking-water reference: WHO (2008). Pyriproxyfen in drinking-water: Use for vector control in drinking-water sources and containers. Background document for the development of WHO Guidelines for drinking-water quality. 20. Delete the following reference: WHO (2010). Pyriproxyfen in drinking-water: Use for vector control in drinking-water sources and containers. 21. On page 463, delete the following references: WHO (2011). Lead in drinking-water. WHO (2011). Nitrate and nitrite in drinking-water. 22. Update the citation from WHO (2011) to WHO (2012) for the Uranium in drinking-water reference. 23. Insert the following reference above Other references cited: WHO (2016). Barium in drinking-water. Background document for the development of WHO Guidelines for drinking-water quality. 24. On page 469, for Bentazone, change the text in the second column to: Occurs in drinking-water or drinking-water sources at concentrations well below those of health concern. 25. Replace the Chlorine dioxide entry with the following: Chlorine dioxide: Reduced primarily to chlorite, chlorate, and chloride in drinking-water, and to chlorite and chloride upon ingestion. The provisional guideline values for chlorite and chlorate are protective for potential toxicity from chlorine dioxide. 26. On page 470, insert the following below the 1,3-Dichloropropane entry: Dichlorvos: Occurs in drinking-water or drinking-water sources at concentrations well below those of health concern. Dicofol: Unlikely to occur in drinking-water or drinking-water sources. 27. Replace the Diquat entry with the following: Diquat: Occurs in drinking-water or drinking-water sources at concentrations well below those of health concern. 28. On page 471, replace the text in the first column next to Manganese with: Not of health concern at levels normally causing acceptability problems in drinking-water. However, there are circumstances where manganese can remain in solution at higher concentrations in some acidic or anaerobic waters, particularly groundwater. 29. Insert the following below the Manganese entry: MCPA: Occurs in drinking-water or drinking-water sources at concentrations well below those of health concern. 30. Change the superscript b on Glyphosate and AMPA to superscript c. 31. On page 472, insert a new footnote b as follows: Although dicofol does not fulfill one of the three criteria for evaluation in the Guidelines, a background document has been prepared and a health-based value has been established in response to a request from Member States for guidance.
